disease_label_per_paper: Serotonin syndrome induced by combined use of sertraline and linezolid
presentation_summary: 82-year-old woman with major depressive disorder had been taking sertraline 100 mg/day for 3-4 years.
She presented with high-grade fever, loose stools, and burning micturition, and was treated for E. coli urinary infection.
On hospital day 3 linezolid was added at 12:30 pm after recurrent fever raised concern for hospital-acquired infection.
At about 1 am she developed altered sensorium, breathlessness, and high fever not responding to antipyretic, requiring ICU transfer.
ICU vitals showed temperature 104.5 F, pulse 126/min, blood pressure 158/72 mmHg, and respiratory rate 50/min.
Neurologic exam showed lower-extremity-predominant rigidity, bilateral patellar hyperreflexia 4+, and Babinski reflexes.
Sertraline and linezolid were stopped and she received aggressive IV hydration; mental status improved within 24 hours and returned to baseline by day 2.

quality_warnings: The urinary infection context is preserved in risk_context/microbiology with use_in_ranking:false because it is a comorbidity/mimic context rather than the serotonin-syndrome diagnostic conclusion.
The case did not report clonus or tremor; the ordinary ranking evidence emphasizes rapid linezolid timing, SSRI exposure, hyperthermia, altered sensorium, rigidity, and hyperreflexia.
